headline: Maui Liquor Commission

meeting.summary: Liquor commissioners accepted a brewery's application despite zoning questions, renewed a wildfire emergency rule, and heard the director will retire December 31.
meeting.recap: The chair called the Liquor Control Commission meeting to order on Wednesday, September 9.[[0:00:36]] Staff said the Planning Department raised new zoning questions about one applicant's planned uses.[[0:29:33]] The applicant's attorney said zoning may not allow selling kegs or cases to stores, restaurants or bars.[[0:31:26]] A motion to go into executive session (a closed-door discussion) about county liability failed.[[1:04:33]] The commission accepted the brewery's application, which must still meet all license requirements, including zoning.[[1:07:05]] The director said he will retire, with December 31 as his last day.[[1:35:14]] Commissioners set a special meeting for September 21 at 1:30 p.m. on hiring a new director.[[1:39:13]] The commission approved an updated application form for special liquor licenses.[[1:54:22]] The commission renewed, for the seventh time, an emergency rule on relocating liquor licenses for premises destroyed in the August 2023 wildfires.[[1:57:56]] Staff will bring an updated draft of the full rule rewrite back next month.[[2:22:59]] Staff will ask Corporation Counsel for legal advice on all forms that require notarization.[[2:42:29]] The commission voted unanimously to go into executive session.[[2:53:03]]
decided: The commission approved the minutes of its August 12, 2026 meeting.
The commission confirmed the department's general licensing matters.
The commission accepted application number one from a sushi restaurant, with the applicant to keep meeting license requirements.
The commission accepted application number two from IP3 LLC, with the applicant to keep meeting license requirements.
The commission accepted application number three for the Maui Beach Ballroom at the Maui Beach Hotel.
The commission accepted application number four, a dining room application from the same company.
The commission accepted application number five for a restaurant liquor license.
A motion to go into executive session to discuss county liability failed.
The commission approved application number 18 for a category BII liquor license.
The commission approved the updated application for a special liquor license, form DLC 016.
The commission approved the seventh reauthorization of the emergency rule on relocating liquor licenses for wildfire-destroyed premises.
The commission voted to go into executive session to continue a discussion from its last meeting.
meeting.next: No liquor license will be issued to the brewery until it meets the zoning clearance requirement. Staff will seek written confirmation on whether a nonprofit tax form can be used as proof of nonprofit status. Commissioners said they would pause new rule changes until the new rule book is adopted. The full rule rewrite will be back on next month's agenda with an updated draft.

moments.q: Brewery's attorney: "we really really request you do not defer this application."
Can nonprofits auction wine trips? "It is not prohibited."
